I. TextPara 1 & Para 2

Para 1▸
The narrator opens with a claim: as a boy he decided that thinking has three grades, and that he himself cannot think at all — the ironic premise of the whole essay.
0:00 / 0:00
While I was still a boy, I came to the conclusion that there were three grades of thinking; and that I myself could not think at all.
Paraphrase
As a child, I decided that thinking came in three levels, and that I was incapable of any thinking.
Full entry →
Translation
当我还是个孩子的时候，我便得出了这样的结论：思考可分三个层次，而我本人则根本不会思考。

Verbal Irony → Sarcasm
Says “I could not think.” Read forward: a modest confession. Read back after Para 23: the judges’ own verdict thrown back at them.

Para 2▸
Three statuettes in the headmaster's study — a lady in a bath towel, a crouching leopard, a miserable naked athlete — first put the subject of thinking before the boy and supply the visual emblems of the three grades.
0:00 / 0:00
It was the headmaster of my grammar school who first brought the subject of thinking before me. He had some statuettes in his study. They stood on a high cupboard behind his desk. One was a lady wearing nothing but a bath towel. She seemed frozen in an eternal panic lest the bath towel slip down any farther; and since she had no arms, she was in an unfortunate position to pull the towel up again. Next to her, crouched the statuette of a leopard, ready to spring down at the top drawer of a filing cabinet. Beyond the leopard was a naked, muscular gentleman, who sat, looking down, with his chin on his fist and his elbow on his knee. He seemed utterly miserable.
Paraphrase
My grammar-school headmaster was the first person to make me think about thinking.
Full entry →
Translation
首先把思考这个问题摆在我面前的是我的小学校长。他的书房里有几尊小雕像，放在他书桌后面高高的柜子上。其中一位是位女士，身上只裹着一条浴巾。她仿佛永远陷在惶恐之中，生怕浴巾再往下滑落分毫；可她偏偏没有双臂，实在没办法把浴巾重新拉上去，处境十分窘迫。在她旁边伏卧着一尊豹子的雕像，一副随时都会扑下来跳到文件柜顶层抽屉上的样子。豹子后面是一个肌肉发达的裸体男子的雕像，他坐在那里，目光朝下，一个拳头托着脸颊，胳膊肘撑在膝上。他看起来愁眉苦脸，一副可怜的样子。

III. Phrases & Collocations10

spring downVerb Phrase
（猛地）向下扑／跃下
to jump or move suddenly and quickly downwards towards sth
TextNext to her, crouched the statuette of a leopard, ready to spring down at the top drawer of a filing cabinet. (Para 2)
E.g.The cat sprang down from the shelf the moment the door opened.　门一开，猫就从架子上跳了下来。
slip downVerb Phrase
滑落；向下滑
to slide downwards out of the proper position
TextShe seemed frozen in an eternal panic lest the bath towel slip down any farther. (Para 2)
E.g.Her mask kept slipping down over her nose.　她的口罩老是滑下来盖住鼻子。
pull upVerb Phrase
向上拉；拉起
to raise or lift sth to a higher position
Text…since she had no arms, she was in an unfortunate position to pull the towel up again. (Para 2)
E.g.He pulled up his socks and walked out.　他提上袜子走了出去。
nothing butPrepositional Phrase
只不过；仅仅
only; nothing except
TextOne was a lady wearing nothing but a bath towel. (Para 2)
E.g.There was nothing but silence in the empty hall.　空荡的大厅里只有一片寂静。
in panicPrepositional Phrase
在恐慌中；惊慌地
in a state of sudden uncontrollable fear
TextShe seemed frozen in an eternal panic lest the bath towel slip down any farther. (Para 2)
E.g.The crowd fled in panic when the fire alarm went off.　火警一响，人群惊慌逃散。
in a positionPrepositional Phrase
处于某种境地；能够（做某事）
in a particular situation, esp. one that enables or prevents doing sth
TextSince she had no arms, she was in an unfortunate position to pull the towel up again. (Para 2)
E.g.I am not in a position to comment on the committee’s decision.　我无权对委员会的决定发表意见。
beyond the leopardPrepositional Phrase
在豹（雕像）的那一边
on the far side of the leopard statuette
TextBeyond the leopard was a naked, muscular gentleman, who sat, looking down… (Para 2)
E.g.Beyond the old church stood a row of lime trees.　老教堂的那一边长着一排椴树。
a grammar schoolNoun Phrase
（英国）文法学校／中学（非大学）
a secondary school with an academic curriculum
TextIt was the headmaster of my grammar school who first brought the subject of thinking before me. (Para 2)
E.g.He was educated at a grammar school in the north of England.　他曾在英格兰北部的一所文法学校就读。
a filing cabinetNoun Phrase
文件柜；档案柜
a piece of office furniture with deep drawers for storing documents
Text…ready to spring down at the top drawer of a filing cabinet. (Para 2)
E.g.Every signed contract was locked in the bottom drawer of the filing cabinet.　每份已签合同都锁在文件柜最下层抽屉里。
a bath towelNoun Phrase
浴巾
a large towel used for drying oneself after a bath
TextOne was a lady wearing nothing but a bath towel. (Para 2)
E.g.She wrapped her wet hair in a bath towel after the shower.　淋浴后她用浴巾裹住湿发。

IV. Paraphrase2

Para 1
While I was still a boy, I came to the conclusion that there were three grades of thinking; and that I myself could not think at all.
As a child, I decided that thinking came in three levels, and that I was incapable of any thinking.
Notes
  • grade 此处作“等级／层次”，非“年级”
  • came to the conclusion 固定搭配“得出结论”
  • not… at all “根本不”，at all 强化否定
Para 2
It was the headmaster of my grammar school who first brought the subject of thinking before me.
My grammar-school headmaster was the first person to make me think about thinking.
Notes
  • grammar school 英国“文法学校／中学”，非大学
  • It was … who … 强调句型，强调主语 the headmaster
  • brought … before me 字面“把…带到我面前”，此处意为“引发我对…的关注”

V. Translation3

Para 1
While I was still a boy, I came to the conclusion that there were three grades of thinking; and that I myself could not think at all.
当我还是个孩子的时候，我便得出了这样的结论：思考可分三个层次，而我本人则根本不会思考。
Notes
  • 层次 ← grades（思考的三个层次，即后文三级思考）
  • 根本不会思考 ← not… at all 的绝对否定，语气强硬
Para 2需背诵
One was a lady wearing nothing but a bath towel. She seemed frozen in an eternal panic lest the bath towel slip down any farther; and since she had no arms, she was in an unfortunate position to pull the towel up again.
其中一位是位女士，身上只裹着一条浴巾。她仿佛永远陷在惶恐之中，生怕浴巾再往下滑落分毫；可她偏偏没有双臂，实在没办法把浴巾重新拉上去，处境十分窘迫。
Para 2
It was the headmaster of my grammar school who first brought the subject of thinking before me. He had some statuettes in his study. They stood on a high cupboard behind his desk. One was a lady wearing nothing but a bath towel. She seemed frozen in an eternal panic lest the bath towel slip down any farther; and since she had no arms, she was in an unfortunate position to pull the towel up again. Next to her, crouched the statuette of a leopard, ready to spring down at the top drawer of a filing cabinet. Beyond the leopard was a naked, muscular gentleman, who sat, looking down, with his chin on his fist and his elbow on his knee. He seemed utterly miserable.
首先把思考这个问题摆在我面前的是我的小学校长。他的书房里有几尊小雕像，放在他书桌后面高高的柜子上。其中一位是位女士，身上只裹着一条浴巾。她仿佛永远陷在惶恐之中，生怕浴巾再往下滑落分毫；可她偏偏没有双臂，实在没办法把浴巾重新拉上去，处境十分窘迫。在她旁边伏卧着一尊豹子的雕像，一副随时都会扑下来跳到文件柜顶层抽屉上的样子。豹子后面是一个肌肉发达的裸体男子的雕像，他坐在那里，目光朝下，一个拳头托着脸颊，胳膊肘撑在膝上。他看起来愁眉苦脸，一副可怜的样子。
Notes
  • 小雕像 ← statuettes，为下文象征意义埋笔
  • 文件柜 ← filing cabinet；本段长句多，宜拆分后顺译
  • 愁眉苦脸 ← miserable 的意译，原文指“可怜／悲惨”

VI. Rhetorical Devices2

Verbal Irony → Sarcasm　反语（回看即讽刺）
While I was still a boy, I came to the conclusion that there were three grades of thinking; and that I myself could not think at all.
Definition: Verbal irony says one thing and means another; sarcasm is verbal irony with a target and the wish to wound.
Verbal irony is the mechanism; sarcasm adds a target. This line is the first — and becomes the second.
ReadingIs a target available?The line reads as
Forward
at Para 1		 No — the headmaster arrives at Para 10, Mr Houghton at Para 16 a self-deprecating confession → verbal irony
Backward
after Para 23		 Yes — the judges are named and convicted their verdict handed back to them → sarcasm
The target is planted in advance: “three grades” implies somebody at the bottom.
You call me unable to think; you turn out to be grade three; what I was doing was thinking.
Key line　“I could not think at all” is verbal irony that turns into sarcasm: not a confession of a defect but a verdict returned — and the essay in your hands is the receipt.
Personification　拟人
She seemed frozen in an eternal panic lest the bath towel slip down any farther.
她似乎凝固在永久的恐惧之中，唯恐浴巾再向下滑。
Definition: Human feelings or actions are attributed to something lifeless.
Analysis: A plaster figure is credited with a human emotion (panic). The humour lies in the boy’s projection: Venus cannot be afraid. Para 3 deflates it at once — “She was not worried about the towel. She was just busy being beautiful.”

VII. Word Differentiationslip / slide / glide

slip / slide / glide　(Para 2, 27)
WordPos.Core meaningUseText / ExampleCollocation
slipv./n.滑倒；滑落；溜走意外、失控地滑（滑倒、滑落）；亦指悄悄移动／放入；常带负面或紧张色彩Para 2：lest the bath towel slip down any farther（浴巾“滑落”，带紧张感）slip on ice／slip down／slip away／slip a note in
slidev./n.（使）滑动，滑行沿表面平稳移动；自觉或自然持续；过去式 slidPara 27：I slid my arm around her waist（顺滑、自觉的动作）slide down／slide into／slide show／let sth. slide
glidev./n.滑翔，轻盈滑行无声、流畅、优雅地移动；多用于飞鸟、舞者、滑雪；富诗意课文中未出现；比 slide 更优雅：glide across the floorglide through the air／glide on skis／glide silently
2. Core Meanings
  1. slip (v./n.) 滑倒；滑落；溜走——意外、失控地滑，或悄悄移动
  2. slide (v./n.)（使）滑动，滑行——沿表面平稳移动，常自觉／持续
  3. glide (v./n.) 滑翔，轻盈滑行——无声、流畅、优雅地移动
3. Key Distinctions
  1. 共同点：都含“滑动”之义，常描写物体或人的移动。
  2. 语义侧重：slip = 失控／意外滑；slide = 沿面平稳滑；glide = 轻盈优雅滑。
  3. 失控 vs 受控：slip 多含“失足、不经意”（slip on a banana skin）；slide / glide 多为有意或自然顺畅的移动。
  4. 语体／意象：glide 最富诗意与优雅感；slide 中性通用；slip 常带负面或悄悄义（slip away 溜走）。
  5. 课文双处呼应：Para 2 浴巾 slip down 的紧张，与 Para 27 叙述者 slid his arm 的轻佻得意，一紧一松，皆以“滑动”写心理。
  6. 搭配辨析：slip on ice／slide down a banister／glide through the air；slip 还可作“悄悄放”（slip a note into…）。
  7. 形近提醒：slip → slipped；slide → slid（Para 27 即用）；glide → glided（规则变化）。
4. Examples
  1. Para 2：…lest the bath towel slip down any farther…　生怕浴巾再往下滑一点……（slip down = 意外滑落）
  2. Para 27：I slid my arm around her waist…　我缓缓揽住她的腰……（slid = slide 过去式，顺滑动作）
  3. She slipped on the wet floor and twisted her ankle.　她在湿地板上滑倒，扭了脚踝。
  4. The children slid down the snowy hill on trays.　孩子们用托盘滑下雪坡。
  5. A swan glided silently across the lake.　一只天鹅静静滑过湖面。
Tip: slip = “失足／滑落”（意外、失控）；slide = “沿面滑行”（自觉、平稳，slid 为过去式）；glide = “轻盈滑翔”（优雅、无声）。
